name: LASKAR
overview: LASKAR (Lambda Cyhalothrin 4.9% CS) is a powerful synthetic pyrethroid insecticide in micro-encapsulated capsule suspension form. It provides prolonged residual activity and superior protection against a wide range of sucking and chewing pests.
description: LASKAR contains Lambda Cyhalothrin 4.9% CS — a third-generation synthetic pyrethroid with excellent knock-down and residual properties. The capsule suspension (CS) formulation ensures controlled release, lower dermal toxicity, and enhanced rainfastness compared to EC formulations. Ideal for cotton, vegetables, and paddy.
key_benefits: Micro-encapsulated CS formulation — safer and more effective
Rapid knock-down with long residual control (14–21 days)
Effective against sucking, chewing, and boring insects
Rainfastness ensures performance even after light showers
Lower mammalian toxicity vs. traditional EC formulations
usage_dosage: 400–600 ml per hectare diluted in 500 L of water. For vegetables: 1–1.5 ml per liter of water.
application_method: Foliar spray. Apply at the first sign of pest infestation. Repeat after 15–21 days if required.
safety_precautions: Wear protective clothing, gloves, mask, and goggles. Do not spray in windy conditions. Harmful if swallowed or inhaled. Keep away from children and livestock.
storage_instructions: Store in original container in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place away from food, feed, and water sources. Keep below 35°C.

faqs.question: What pests does LASKAR control?
faqs.answer: LASKAR controls aphids, whiteflies, thrips, bollworms, leaf hoppers, armyworms, and other chewing/sucking insects.

faqs.question: What is the pre-harvest interval (PHI)?
faqs.answer: Observe a minimum 7-day PHI before harvest for vegetables and 15 days for cotton.

faqs.question: Is LASKAR rainfast?
faqs.answer: Yes, the CS formulation provides rainfastness within 2 hours of application.

faqs.question: Can it be tank-mixed?
faqs.answer: Compatible with most insecticides and fungicides. Always test compatibility in a small quantity before mixing.

name: KILL-71
overview: KILL-71 (Ammonium Salt of Glyphosate 71% SG) is a highly concentrated, non-selective, systemic herbicide. It controls a broad spectrum of annual and perennial grasses, sedges, and broad-leaved weeds.
description: KILL-71 is a water-soluble granule (SG) formulation of Ammonium Salt of Glyphosate 71% — among the highest concentrations available. Being systemic, it is absorbed through foliage and translocated to roots, killing the entire weed including root system. Used for pre-planting weed control and in plantation crops.
key_benefits: Ultra-high concentration — 71% SG, economical to use
Complete systemic action kills weeds root to tip
Controls over 200 weed species including grasses and broadleaf
Soil inactivation — does not affect subsequent crops
Water-soluble granule: easy to handle, measure, and mix
usage_dosage: 625–1250 gm per hectare in 250–500 L of water depending on weed density and species.
application_method: Directed spray on actively growing weeds. Do NOT allow spray to contact crop plants. Use a hood or shield sprayer near crops.
safety_precautions: Non-selective — will kill any green plant it contacts. Wear full protective gear. Do not spray on windy days. Keep away from water bodies.
storage_instructions: Store in dry, cool place in original sealed container. Keep away from food and animal feed. Do not store near fertilizers.

faqs.question: Is KILL-71 safe for subsequent crops?
faqs.answer: Yes. Glyphosate is inactivated upon contact with soil, so it does not affect crops planted after application.

faqs.question: How long after application can I sow?
faqs.answer: Wait 3–7 days after spraying before planting depending on weed density.

faqs.question: Will rain affect efficacy?
faqs.answer: Rain within 6 hours of application may reduce efficacy. Re-apply if heavy rain occurs.

name: CHITRAZINE
overview: CHITRAZINE (Atrazine 50% WP) is a selective, systemic, pre- and post-emergent herbicide for effective control of annual grasses and broad-leaved weeds in maize, sugarcane, and sorghum crops.
description: CHITRAZINE contains Atrazine 50% WP — a triazine herbicide that inhibits photosynthesis in susceptible plants. It is absorbed by roots and foliage and is translocated upward. Effective as both pre-emergent and early post-emergent treatment, providing season-long weed control in maize and sugarcane.
key_benefits: Dual action — pre-emergent and early post-emergent control
Provides season-long weed control in one application
Controls grasses, sedges, and broad-leaved weeds
Cost-effective WP formulation — easy to measure and mix
Reduces labour cost of manual weeding significantly
usage_dosage: 1–2 kg per hectare in 500 L of water. Apply as pre-emergent within 3 days of sowing or early post-emergent up to 3-leaf stage of weeds.
application_method: Pre-emergent: Spray on moist soil immediately after sowing. Post-emergent: Spray on 2–3 leaf stage weeds. Use flat fan nozzle for even coverage.
safety_precautions: Do not use on sandy soils with low organic matter. Highly toxic to aquatic organisms. Keep away from water bodies, fish ponds, and drainage channels.
storage_instructions: Store in original container in cool, dry, well-ventilated store. Shelf life: 2 years from date of manufacture.

faqs.question: Is CHITRAZINE safe for maize?
faqs.answer: Yes, maize has inherent tolerance to Atrazine at recommended doses. Avoid use on maize varieties with known sensitivity.

faqs.question: Can CHITRAZINE be used in paddy?
faqs.answer: No. CHITRAZINE should not be used in paddy/rice fields as it will damage the crop.

faqs.question: What weeds does it control?
faqs.answer: Controls Amaranthus, Chenopodium, Digitaria, Echinochloa, Cynodon, and most common annual weeds.

name: JORAWAR
overview: JORAWAR (Azoxystrobin 11% + Tebuconazole 18.3% SC) is a premium combination fungicide offering curative and preventive action against a wide spectrum of fungal diseases in field crops and vegetables.
description: JORAWAR combines two powerful fungicides: Azoxystrobin (strobilurin group) which inhibits mitochondrial respiration, and Tebuconazole (triazole group) which inhibits ergosterol biosynthesis. This dual mode of action provides broad-spectrum control with low risk of resistance development.
key_benefits: Dual mode of action — strobilurin + triazole combination
Controls blast, rust, blight, powdery mildew, and sheath blight
SC formulation — superior rainfastness and crop safety
Extended protection period of 14–21 days per spray
usage_dosage: 300–500 ml per hectare in 500 L of water. Start at first sign of disease. Repeat at 14-day intervals.
application_method: Foliar spray. Apply during early morning or late evening. Ensure complete coverage of foliage, especially the underside of leaves.
safety_precautions: Wear mask, gloves, and full protective clothing. Do not allow spray to drift to neighbouring crops. Wash hands and exposed skin after application.
storage_instructions: Store between 5–35°C in original container. Avoid freezing. Keep away from fire sources. Shelf life: 2 years.

faqs.question: When should JORAWAR first be applied?
faqs.answer: Apply preventively at the first sign of disease, or before disease onset in high-risk conditions.

faqs.question: How many sprays are recommended?
faqs.answer: 2–3 sprays per season at 14-day intervals provide effective disease control.

faqs.question: Is it safe on grapes?
faqs.answer: Yes, JORAWAR is effective against downy mildew and powdery mildew on grapes.

name: KRANTIKARI
overview: KRANTIKARI (Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC) is a broad-spectrum systemic fungicide with dual active ingredients providing superior protection against major fungal diseases in vegetables, cereals, and fruits.
description: KRANTIKARI's combination of Azoxystrobin and Difenoconazole delivers both protective and curative action. Azoxystrobin arrests fungal spore germination while Difenoconazole stops mycelial growth and sporulation. Together, they provide comprehensive protection against early and late blight, alternaria, cercospora, and anthracnose.
key_benefits: Curative action up to 48 hours after infection
Excellent systemic distribution — protects new growth
Minimizes yield loss from fungal diseases significantly
usage_dosage: 200–300 ml per hectare. Dilute in 200–500 L of water. Apply at 7–14 day intervals.
application_method: Foliar spray. Ensure thorough coverage. Begin application at early disease stage. Use sufficient water volume for complete leaf coverage.
safety_precautions: Mildly irritating to eyes. Wear protective goggles and gloves. Store away from food. Do not mix with alkaline pesticides.
storage_instructions: Store in original container at room temperature (below 35°C). Do not freeze. Shelf life: 2 years.

faqs.question: What diseases does KRANTIKARI control?
faqs.answer: Controls early blight, late blight, powdery mildew, downy mildew, anthracnose, cercospora leaf spot, and rust.

faqs.question: Can I use KRANTIKARI in tomato?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is highly effective against early and late blight in tomato.

faqs.question: Is KRANTIKARI safe for organic farming?
faqs.answer: No, KRANTIKARI contains synthetic fungicides and is not approved for organic farming.

name: KARGIL-75
overview: KARGIL-75 is a powerful combination of Carbendazim 12% and Mancozeb 63% WP. It provides dual action—systemic and contact—to control a wide range of fungal diseases.
description: KARGIL-75 (Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP) is a broad-spectrum, contact and systemic fungicide which controls many fungal diseases in field crops and vegetables. It is very effective for controlling diseases like blast, rust, and leaf spots.
key_benefits: Dual action: Systemic and Contact protection
Broad spectrum control over many fungal pathogens
usage_dosage: 2-3 gm per liter of water. Suitable for foliar spray and seed treatment.
safety_precautions: Wear protective clothing. Avoid inhalation and contact with skin/eyes. Wash thoroughly after use.
storage_instructions: Store in a cool, dry place away from children and foodstuff.

faqs.question: Is it safe for all crops?
faqs.answer: It is generally safe for most crops when used at recommended dosages.

faqs.question: What is the pack size?
faqs.answer: Available in 500gm packs.

name: VANDAN
overview: VANDAN contains Carbendazim 46.27% SC. It is a systemic fungicide with both preventive and curative action against a variety of fungal diseases.
description: VANDAN (Carbendazim 46.27% SC) is a highly effective systemic fungicide used to control wilt, damping off, and other fungal diseases. The SC formulation ensures better coverage and efficacy.
key_benefits: Effective against a wide range of soil-borne and foliar diseases
usage_dosage: 1-2 ml per liter of water. Can be used for foliar spray or soil drenching.
safety_precautions: Follow standard safety protocols. Keep away from water sources.
storage_instructions: Keep in original container in a cool, well-ventilated area.

faqs.question: Can I use it for soil drenching?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is very effective for soil drenching to control wilt.

faqs.question: What is the pack size?
faqs.answer: Available in 1L packs.

name: FUNGASTIN
overview: FUNGASTIN is a high-quality Carbendazim 50% WP fungicide. It is a systemic fungicide used globally for effective disease management.
description: FUNGASTIN (Carbendazim 50% WP) provides excellent control over a broad range of fungal diseases including powdery mildew and scab. It is a cornerstone for disease management in many crops.
key_benefits: Strong systemic movement within the plant
usage_dosage: 2 gm per liter of water. Best for foliar spray and seed treatment.
safety_precautions: Do not eat, drink or smoke during application. Use protective gear.
storage_instructions: Store securely away from food and moisture.

faqs.question: What is the active ingredient?
faqs.answer: Carbendazim 50% WP.

faqs.question: Is it good for seed treatment?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is highly recommended for seed treatment.

name: FEURADON-3G
overview: FEURADON-3G (Carbofuran 3% CG) is a granular systemic insecticide and nematicide for soil application.
description: FEURADON-3G is a soil-applied granular insecticide that provides long-term protection against soil insects and nematodes. It is absorbed by the roots and translocated to the rest of the plant.
key_benefits: Broad-spectrum control of soil insects and nematodes
Safe for crops when applied to soil
Improves root health and plant vigor
usage_dosage: 5-10 kg per acre depending on crop and pest pressure.
safety_precautions: EXTREMELY TOXIC. Handle with extreme care. Wear full protective gear. Avoid skin contact.
storage_instructions: Store in a locked, dry place away from food and feed.

faqs.question: Is it applied to leaves?
faqs.answer: No, it is strictly for soil application.

faqs.question: What pests does it control?
faqs.answer: Termites, nematodes, stem borers, and other soil pests.

name: ATTACK-20
overview: ATTACK-20 contains Chlorpyriphos 20% EC. It is a versatile insecticide used for both foliar and soil treatments.
description: ATTACK-20 (Chlorpyriphos 20% EC) is effective against a wide range of sucking and chewing insects. It is particularly well-known for its efficacy against termites in both agricultural and non-agricultural settings.
key_benefits: Triple action: Contact, Stomach, and Vapor action
usage_dosage: 2.5 ml per liter for foliar spray. For termite control, use 5-10 ml per liter for soil treatment.
safety_precautions: Toxic to fish and bees. Avoid spraying near water bodies. Use mask and gloves.
storage_instructions: Store in cool, dry place. Keep away from fire and direct sunlight.

faqs.question: Can it be used for termites?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is one of the best treatments for termite control.

faqs.question: What is the concentration?
faqs.answer: Chlorpyriphos 20% EC.

name: ATTACK-505
overview: ATTACK-505 is a powerful combination of Chlorpyriphos 50% and Cypermethrin 5% EC. It provides a synergistic effect against tough-to-control pests.
description: ATTACK-505 (Chlorpyriphos 50% + Cypermethrin 5% EC) is an insecticide that combines two different modes of action to provide comprehensive control over bollworms, borers, and sucking pests.
key_benefits: Synergistic action for better pest control
usage_dosage: 2 ml per liter of water for foliar application.
safety_precautions: Highly flammable. Use with caution. Wear full protective clothing.
storage_instructions: Store in a cool place away from any heat source.

faqs.question: What is special about 505?
faqs.answer: The combination of Chlorpyriphos and Cypermethrin makes it much stronger against resistant pests.

faqs.question: What crops is it for?
faqs.answer: Highly recommended for Cotton and Vegetables.

name: CHITRA-COC
overview: CHITRA-COC (Copper Oxychloride 50% WP) is a broad-spectrum inorganic fungicide with excellent preventive action.
description: CHITRA-COC is a traditional and highly reliable fungicide used to control various diseases like blights, leaf spots, and mildews. It is known for its excellent stickiness and rainfastness.
key_benefits: Broad-spectrum control over many bacterial and fungal diseases
Safe for the environment when used correctly
usage_dosage: 2.5-3 gm per liter of water for foliar spray.
safety_precautions: Do not mix with lime sulfur or dithiocarbamates. Use PPE.
storage_instructions: Store in a dry place. Protect from moisture.

faqs.question: Does it control bacterial diseases?
faqs.answer: Yes, Copper Oxychloride is effective against several bacterial blights.

faqs.question: Can it be used on grapes?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is commonly used to control downy mildew in grapes.

name: CYMO PLUS
overview: CYMO PLUS is a combination of Cymoxanil 8% and Mancozeb 64% WP. It is a specialist for downy mildew and late blight.
description: CYMO PLUS (Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP) provides systemic and contact action. Cymoxanil penetrates the leaves quickly to stop existing infections, while Mancozeb provides a protective barrier on the surface.
key_benefits: Specific control for Downy Mildew and Late Blight
usage_dosage: 2.5 gm per liter of water for foliar application.
safety_precautions: Apply during early symptoms. Avoid spraying in high winds.
storage_instructions: Keep in a cool, dry place away from children.

faqs.question: Is it good for late blight?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is one of the most effective treatments for Late Blight in Potato and Tomato.

faqs.question: How does it work?
faqs.answer: It has dual action: it stops existing fungal growth and prevents new spores from germinating.

name: CHITGOR
overview: CHITGOR (Dimethoate 30% EC) is a highly effective organophosphate insecticide with systemic and contact action.
description: CHITGOR is a widely used insecticide for the control of a broad range of sucking pests and mites. Its systemic action ensures that pests feeding on any part of the plant are controlled.
key_benefits: Effective against sucking pests like aphids, thrips, and mites
Widely used in agriculture and horticulture
usage_dosage: 2 ml per liter of water for foliar application.
safety_precautions: Toxic to birds and bees. Avoid use during flowering. Use proper protective equipment.
storage_instructions: Store in a cool place away from children and pets.

faqs.question: What pests does it control?
faqs.answer: Mainly aphids, thrips, whiteflies, and mites.

faqs.question: Is it systemic?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is a strong systemic insecticide.

name: BENZO FIRE
overview: BENZO FIRE contains Emamectin Benzoate 1.9% EC. It is a modern insecticide specifically designed for lepidopteran pests.
description: BENZO FIRE (Emamectin Benzoate 1.9% EC) is a highly potent insecticide that works by disrupting the nervous system of caterpillars. It is effective even at low dosages and is safer for many beneficial insects.
key_benefits: Translaminar activity—controls pests on the underside of leaves
usage_dosage: 1 ml per liter of water for foliar application.
safety_precautions: Avoid spray drift. Wear protective gear. Store in original container.
storage_instructions: Keep in a cool, dark, and dry place.

faqs.question: Is it effective against bollworms?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is highly effective against American and Spotted Bollworms.

faqs.question: Does it work on the underside of leaves?
faqs.answer: Yes, its translaminar action allows it to move through the leaf.
